head: 73cca9c8d5ec3ec85530ef9fa476bf8b37ee870e
summary: Access control, tenant isolation and the concurrency design hold up under attack: no p_firm argument anywhere, CLR04 for bookkeeper/viewer/removed/non-member, 42501 for clara_runtime / clara_agent_ro / both wake roles, the ceiling function reachable by nobody, a real two-session race that serialises correctly on the advisory lock with consistent before-images, and no existence oracle in any new refusal. The sharp defect is elsewhere: #960's op key is a pure function of (caller, the four integers) with no nonce, and clara.op_receipts never expires, so a cap value a person set once can never be set again by that person -- the door replays the ORIGINAL receipt, the card renders a false 'Saved ... 8 documents at once' from it and clears the person's typed value, while the stored cap does not move. Proven live on clara_l10. Three further defects: the invitee-facing issuer_lapsed notice promises 'accepting is unaffected' where accept_invite refuses CLR04 (proven for a removed issuer at the LOWEST role and for a demoted issuer below the invited role); #1003's 0271 ships no preintegration gate and no bimodal cohort, so two test-side edits hard-FAIL rather than skip on any chain below 0271 (proven in a rolled-back transaction); and #872's readiness predicate keys on the migration NUMBER '^0269_' rather than a stable stem, contradicting the work order and the sibling gate the same lane wrote for 0270 (proven in a rolled-back transaction). #871 produced no code and its stop is well-evidenced (grep for service_role across packages/db/migrations returns 0; docs/ARCHITECTURE.md contains no 'invit' at all, which also backs #872's deviation).

findings.title: The deterministic cap op key makes any repeat of an earlier edit a permanent no-op that the card reports as a successful save
findings.evidence: apps/web/lib/firm/capacity-doors.ts:processingCapsOpKey builds `op-caps-${callerId}-${docs}-${pages}-${ocr}-${witness}` with no nonce, no timestamp and no free-text component (the door has none to bind); apps/web/components/firm-admin/firm-settings-panel.tsx:saveCaps passes processingCapsOpKey(scope.user_id ?? '', e). clara._reserve_op keys replay on (firm, fn, op_key) and re-hashes the arguments; clara.op_receipts rows never expire. PROVEN LIVE on 127.0.0.1:55750/clara_l10 (scratch probe, firm b2a1f906-562e-46db-a09b-239d2b9645d7, owner eef12b07-22e9-4b00-bfb6-328399987201): STEP1 set ocr_concurrency=8 under key `op-caps-<owner>-x-x-8-x` -> receipt caps.ocr_concurrency=8, created=true; STEP2 set ocr_concurrency=2 under a different key -> stored row {docs 100, pages 1000, ocr 2, witness 2}; STEP3 set ocr_concurrency=8 again, which is EXACTLY the key the card re-mints for the same person and the same edit -> the door returned {"status":"set","caps":{..."ocr_concurrency":8...},"changed":[all four],"created":true,"previous":{all null},"updated_at":"...16:09:33.000748+08:00"} -- byte-identical to STEP1's receipt, minted 6ms earlier -- and the STORED row after STEP3 was still {docs 100, pages 1000, ocr 2, witness 2}. No write, no clara.audit_log row. The surface then lies twice: processing-capacity-card.tsx renders `capacityReceipt` from outcome.caps ("Saved. This firm now processes up to ... 8 documents at once") and runs `if (answer.kind === "set") setTyped({})`, discarding the person's number, while firm-settings-panel's unconditional re-read repaints the figures at 2. The person cannot recover: every retry mints the same key. This is exactly the trap apps/web/lib/operator/op-key.ts's own header names ("because the key is deterministic there is no way for the person to pick a different one -- that exact change becomes permanently unsubmittable"); the operator builders escape it only because they bind a free-text reason, which this door does not have. Nothing catches it: lib/firm/capacity-doors.test.ts:142-158 pins the key's stability as intended behaviour, and the e2e fixture installCapacityPair (apps/web/e2e/firm-commercial-walk.spec.ts) ignores p_op_key entirely, so the browser walk cannot see it.
findings.required_fix: Make the operation identity distinguish two genuinely different submissions of the same value. The minimal shape consistent with the house contract is to fold the before-image the page is editing from into the key (e.g. `op-caps-${callerId}-${previousSpelled}-${nextSpelled}`, which stays deterministic for a retry of the SAME submission and differs the moment the stored value has moved), or to carry a per-submission token the card keeps across retries and drops on a new edit. Whatever is chosen, the card must also stop reporting a receipt it did not earn: treat `created===true` on a firm that already had a row, or a receipt whose `updated_at` predates the read the page started from, as a replay and re-read rather than render `capacityReceipt`. Add a cell that drives set(8) -> set(2) -> set(8) through the door and asserts the third call MOVES the stored cap.

findings.title: The invitee's issuer_lapsed notice states acceptance is unaffected, but accept_invite refuses CLR04 for a removed issuer at every role and for a demoted issuer below the invited role
findings.evidence: apps/web/messages/en.json Invite.preview.issuerLapsedNote: "Whoever sent this invitation is no longer an admin or owner there. You can still continue -- accepting is unaffected." INVITE_PREVIEW_NON_BLOCKING_STATUSES makes issuer_lapsed keep the password form open (apps/web/lib/firm/invite-preview.ts, apps/web/components/invite-accept-form.tsx). issuer_lapsed is true exactly when the issuer's current active rank < role_rank('admin')=2; clara.accept_invite refuses when role_rank(invite.role) > coalesce(issuer_rank,-1). Those two conditions overlap over most of the domain. PROVEN LIVE on clara_l10 (scratch probe, four scenarios through the real doors): [healthy-viewer] preview=pending, roster=pending, accept ACCEPTED; [demoted-viewer] preview=issuer_lapsed, roster=issuer_lapsed, accept ACCEPTED; [demoted-adminrole] preview=issuer_lapsed, accept REFUSED CLR04 "invite exceeds the issuer's rank -- re-issue by an owner"; [removed-viewer] preview=issuer_lapsed, accept REFUSED CLR04, at the LOWEST role there is, because coalesce(NULL,-1)=-1 and role_rank('viewer')=0 > -1. So a removed issuer makes EVERY invite unacceptable while the preview tells the invitee the opposite. The harm is not only the wrong sentence: invite-accept-form.tsx:handleSetPassword runs `supabase.auth.updateUser({ password })` and only THEN calls acceptInvite, so the person commits an irreversible account change on the strength of the notice and is then shown the database's raw internal sentence with no membership. The lane's own report names the removed-issuer refusal but does not connect it to the copy it shipped; the web cell p872.web.preview_issuer_lapsed drives only the demoted-compatible case.
findings.required_fix: Stop asserting a fact the accept door does not guarantee. Either (a) reword Invite.preview.issuerLapsedNote to say only what is true for every issuer_lapsed invite -- the issuer no longer holds admin standing, and the firm will re-check whether this invitation can still be accepted when you finish -- or (b) let the preview answer the question it already has the facts for: clara.preview_invite knows the invited role and the issuer's current rank, so it can report whether accept_invite's wall would fire and the form can say 'ask an admin there to re-issue this' instead of walking the person to a password. Add a cell that drives the REMOVED-issuer case end to end through InviteAcceptForm and asserts the surface does not promise acceptance.

findings.title: 0271 ships no preintegration gate and no bimodal cohort, so two test-side edits hard-fail instead of skipping on any chain below it
findings.evidence: The work order's wave-2 addendum requires every migration to ship "a preintegration gate module with a stable stem, a rig-meta cohort, the gate-chain entry in migration order". 0271 ships none of the three (packages/db/package.json's gate chain gained only invite-issuer-lapsed and firm-document-limits-writer; there is no retire-create-account-set gate on disk), while both siblings in this same lane do. The two edits it made instead are unconditional: (1) packages/db/tests/client-financial-pack.test.mjs's p660.census.pins_unmoved now asserts `to_regprocedure('clara.create_account_set_v1(...)') is null` behind a gate() that keys on the 0232 stem, not on 0271; (2) packages/db/tests/rig-meta.mjs removed create_account_set_v1 from METRICS_0058_HUMAN_FNS/ALLOWED, a static import-time constant with no bimodal arm, which grantMatrixFailures() (rig-meta.mjs:3295-3304) compares against the LIVE catalog. PROVEN inside a transaction I rolled back on clara_l10: with the pre-0271 catalog state recreated (create function + grant execute to clara_authenticated), has_function_privilege('clara_authenticated', ...) = true while ALLOWED.clara_authenticated.has('create_account_set_v1') = false, i.e. grantMatrixFailures() reports "clara_authenticated EXECUTE clara.create_account_set_v1: expected false, got true" (operation-census.test.mjs opcen.1 and rig-isolation.test.mjs T17 both consume it), and `to_regprocedure(...) is null` returned FALSE, i.e. p660.census.pins_unmoved's new assertion fails. Rolled back; the function is absent again. Reachable frontiers: rig-meta's own #960 block asserts "the db-slice-frontiers matrix runs this package against earlier frontiers", any lane or reviewer rig standing below 0271, and any manual estate sweep against main. The lane's own report flags this as unresolved and unverified rather than fixing it.
findings.required_fix: Ship the gate 0271 owes: a retire-create-account-set-preintegration-gate.mjs with a STEM-based readiness probe (version ~ 'retire_create_account_set_v1$') and its --import token appended in migration order to packages/db/package.json, plus the matching test-side skip in client-financial-pack.test.mjs so the new to_regprocedure assertion runs only above the 0271 frontier. Give rig-meta.mjs the same bimodal treatment the 0270 cohort already has: keep create_account_set_v1 in ALLOWED[clara_authenticated] while it is still live in the catalog, and drop it only when it is gone, so a pre-0271 frontier skips rather than reporting an unattributed grant.

findings.title: #872's readiness predicate keys on the migration NUMBER, not a stable stem, so a merge-time renumber turns its cells into silent skips
findings.evidence: packages/db/tests/preview-invite.test.mjs's before() hook and unready872() both probe `select 1 from clara.schema_migrations where version ~ '^0269_'`, and tests/invite-issuer-lapsed-preintegration-gate.mjs documents that choice. The sibling gate the SAME lane wrote one ticket later says the opposite in as many words: tests/firm-document-limits-writer-preintegration-gate.mjs -- "readiness is detected off clara.schema_migrations (a row matching the stem firm_document_limits_writer$), never off a migration NUMBER -- numbers are claimed at merge" -- and the work order's addendum asks for "a preintegration gate module with a stable stem". The house idiom agrees: every other readiness probe in packages/db/tests uses a stem$ regex (accounting-plans-fixtures.mjs, accrual-adjustments-fixtures.mjs, activity-feed.test.mjs, chat-clarify-expiry-fixtures.mjs, checkout-convergence-fixtures.mjs, a21-watch.test.mjs, ...). PROVEN inside a transaction I rolled back on clara_l10: the live row is 0269_invite_issuer_lapsed_status; `version ~ '^0269_'` matches 1 before a renumber and 0 after renaming the row to 0277_invite_issuer_lapsed_status, while `version ~ 'invite_issuer_lapsed_status$'` still matches 1. Rolled back; the row is unchanged. Consequence after any merge-time renumber: in an estate sweep (gate preloaded, CLARA_ALLOW_MISSING_ISSUER_LAPSED=1) the four #872 cells -- p872.status.demoted, p872.status.removed, p872.accept.lapsed_but_compatible and the rewritten p625.preview.issuer_rank -- SKIP GREEN against a database where the behaviour is live and could have regressed, which is the exact 'a skip is not evidence' failure packages/db/tests/README.md and tests/preintegration-gate-chain.test.mjs's header both exist to prevent; in a focused run it hard-fails with a message naming a migration that is on disk and applied.
findings.required_fix: Change both probes in preview-invite.test.mjs to the stem `version ~ 'invite_issuer_lapsed_status$'` and correct the gate module's header to match its 0270 sibling. No behaviour or migration change is needed.

findings.title: A cap above int4 range leaves the door as a raw 22003 the card reports as 'could not be sent, so nothing was saved'
findings.evidence: clara.set_firm_document_limits takes int arguments and checks the ceiling only after the cast, so an out-of-range value dies in the cast. PROVEN LIVE on clara_l10: set_firm_document_limits(p_docs_per_day=>2147483648, ...) -> REFUSED 22003 "value 2147483648 is out of range for type integer" with no detail (compare the in-range case, which gives the honest CLR10 "docs_per_day may not exceed the estate ceiling of 10000" detail={"reason":"cap_above_ceiling"}). The card has no upper-bound guard -- processing-capacity-card.tsx accepts anything passing Number.isInteger(parsed) && parsed > 0 -- and apps/web/lib/wire.ts:parseClrCode only recognises a CLR-shaped SQLSTATE, so 22003 becomes a WireError, setFirmDocumentLimits returns { kind: 'unavailable' }, and the banner reads capacityUnavailable: "That change could not be sent, so nothing was saved. Try again." That is false on both halves -- it WAS sent and it WAS refused -- and it invites a retry that can never succeed.
findings.required_fix: Bound the cap arguments before the cast, or declare them bigint and keep the existing v_asked > ceiling check, so every number a caller can type leaves the door as a typed CLR10 with detail.reason='cap_above_ceiling'. A client-side max is a courtesy on top, not a substitute.

findings.title: The CLR13 operation_in_flight arm of the cap door is unreachable, and the migration's tail census and the app's refusal map both enshrine it
findings.evidence: The door raises CLR13 detail.reason='operation_in_flight' when clara._reserve_op returns {'pending': true}, i.e. when an op_receipts row exists with a NULL result. Every call runs in one transaction, so a row is either invisible (uncommitted) or already carries its _finish_op result. PROVEN LIVE with two real connections on clara_l10: session 1 opened a transaction and called the door with key K (receipt minted, transaction held open); session 2 called with the SAME key and BLOCKED on _reserve_op's `on conflict do nothing` speculative insert for the whole 800ms session 1 was held, then -- after session 1 committed -- returned the settled receipt verbatim (waitedMs 804, status 'set'). CLR13 never fired, and op_receipts ended with one row whose result is non-null. The dead arm is then pinned as live in three places: migration 0270 section D's census counts "the door raises exactly 6 times and carries exactly 6 detail.reason payloads", apps/web/lib/firm/capacity-doors.ts's header documents the CLR13 mapping, and the #960 successor contract lists 'CLR13 operation_in_flight -> the same change is already being recorded, wait and re-read' for the wave-4 chat tool. This is speculative code by the work order's own rule 4.
findings.required_fix: Either drop the CLR13 arm (and the corresponding count in section D's census, the entry in capacity-doors.ts's refusal map and the line in the successor contract), or write the cell that reaches it; a branch nothing can observe should not be documented to a future tool author as a refusal it must handle.

findings.title: The estate ceiling bounds one firm, not the estate, so the header's shared-machine justification does not hold across firms
findings.evidence: Migration 0270 section A justifies ocr_concurrency/llm_witness_concurrency = 16 as being "there so that a firm cannot write a number that would queue unbounded vendor calls against a shared machine", on the stated fact that the estate runs ONE always-on clara-runtime machine. But the enforcement is per-firm only: clara.claim_document_processing_task counts `select count(*) into v_running from clara.document_processing_tasks where firm_id=t.firm_id and lane in ('ocr','invoice_facts','statement_facts') and status='running'` against coalesce(l.ocr_concurrency,2), with no estate-wide counter anywhere in that body (read live from pg_proc on clara_l10). Before this ticket every firm sat at the 2/2 fallback because the relation had no human writer at all; after it, every firm can self-serve an 8x raise, and N firms at 16 give 16N concurrent tasks against the one machine with no backstop. The owner's ruling says "the estate's own safety limits stay the absolute ceiling above whatever a firm sets" -- as built, that ceiling is per-firm.
findings.required_fix: Say in the header what the ceiling actually bounds (one firm's share, not the estate's total), and file the estate-wide backstop as its own follow-up so the owner can rule on it; nothing in this ticket's acceptance criteria is broken, but the justification as written is stronger than the code.

findings.title: The delta-contract 60/60 evidence does not reproduce on the lane database (58 pass / 2 fail) -- by that suite's own fresh-database contract, not a lane defect
findings.evidence: I re-ran `node --test --test-concurrency=1 $GATES tests/delta-contract.test.mjs` with the full 104-gate chain against 127.0.0.1:55750/clara_l10, twice: 60 tests, 58 pass, 2 fail both times. The failing cell is delta-catalog-phase.mjs:633 "freeze verifier positively reads registered live bodies, deployment count exact for either witness shape" -- verified_deployed 6 !== expected 5 -- and the second failure is only its parent rolling up. The cause is outside this lane's diff: clara.evaluator_versions on this rig carries 8 registered closures of which 6 are deployed, and the sixth is prepayment_schedule v1, which that cell's `5 + fsPackDeployed + card1V2Deployed` arithmetic does not know about; the cell is masked on a FRESH database because evaluatorCeremonyUnwitnessed() then short-circuits to 0. The parent test is literally titled "delta contract requires a fresh disposable DB and runs its one-way ceremony in order", so this is the suite's documented re-run contract. Recorded because #1003's AC5 rests wholly on that suite and the claim cannot be re-verified on the lane rig once the one-way ceremony has run; every other claim in the lane's four reports that I re-ran DID reproduce (firm-document-limits-writer.test.mjs 9/9 and preview-invite.test.mjs 15/15 under the full gate chain; compliance-register-panel 4/4, processing-capacity-card 5/5, capacity-doors 4/4, members-tables 3/3, firm-admin compliance 16/16, firm-settings-panel 6/6, e2e-fixture-ownership 44/44).
findings.required_fix: The integrator must run delta-contract.test.mjs on a disposable, never-ceremonied database to re-establish #1003's AC5; it cannot be re-proved on clara_l10. Worth a separate ticket for delta-catalog-phase.mjs:654, whose deployed-count arithmetic is stale against the current registered set.

findings.title: processingCapsOpKey falls back to an empty caller id, which two admins would share and both then lose permanently
findings.evidence: apps/web/components/firm-admin/firm-settings-panel.tsx:saveCaps calls processingCapsOpKey(scope.user_id ?? '', e). FirmScopeValue is `NavigationScope & Partial<Pick<CallerContextRow, 'firm_name'|'role'|'firm_id'|'user_id'>>` (apps/web/components/firm-scope-provider.tsx:50), so user_id is optional in the type; the provider's own header says "Production always passes the full row", which is a claim about callers, not a guarantee the type carries. If it were ever absent, two admins making the same edit would both mint `op-caps--<spelled>`, and because clara._reserve_op folds the actor into the re-hashed arguments the second would meet CLR10 op_key_conflict -- permanently, since the key is deterministic and op_receipts never expires. capacity-doors.ts's own header gives folding the caller in as the reason this cannot happen; the `?? ''` fallback quietly undoes it.
findings.required_fix: Do not offer the control when scope.user_id is absent (the card already degrades to read-only when `save` is undefined), or throw rather than mint a key under an empty caller id -- a save that cannot be attributed should not be attempted.

attacks_run_that_found_nothing: Cross-tenant reach on clara.set_firm_document_limits: the door takes no p_firm and derives the firm from clara._human_ctx; a second firm created in the same probe kept zero firm_document_limits rows throughout.

Rank floors on the new door: bookkeeper CLR04 'insufficient role', viewer CLR04 'insufficient role', a person with no membership CLR04 'actor has no active membership', an admin whose membership was REMOVED mid-probe CLR04 'actor has no active membership'; an admin (rank 2, not the owner) succeeds.

Role reach: clara_runtime, clara_agent_ro, clara_wake_interactive and clara_wake_proactive all get 42501 on set_firm_document_limits; clara._firm_document_limit_ceiling is 42501 for clara_authenticated, clara_runtime and clara_agent_ro alike (granted to nobody).

Bounds: each cap ACCEPTED exactly at its ceiling (10000/100000/16/16) and refused at ceiling+1 with CLR10 cap_above_ceiling naming the number; 0 and -3 refused CLR10 invalid_cap; a call naming no cap refused CLR10 no_cap_named; a null op key refused CLR10 invalid_op_key.

Two-session race on the cap door with two real connections: the second writer waited 417ms on the per-firm advisory lock and its receipt's `previous` carried the FIRST writer's committed value (docs 500), the first's carried the pre-race value (docs 100); the final row held both changes and neither receipt claimed a before-image the other contradicts. Lock order is op_receipts -> advisory -> row FOR UPDATE, the same in every path, and the advisory key sits in the single-bigint space while the ingest lane's is the two-int form, so the two cannot alias.

Silent collateral on a first cap write: the trigger's first-insert values (100/1000/2/2) are byte-equal to the fallbacks every enforcing door coalesces to (_reserve_document_ingest 100/1000, claim_document_processing_task 2/2, the three settle/resize doors 1000), so naming one cap does not move a firm's effective limits on the others.

issuer_lapsed as a cross-tenant membership oracle: 0269 uses a correlated subquery, not a granted helper; clara._invite_issuer_rank is absent; clara.firm_memberships' grant matrix is byte-identical before and after (clara_agent_ro:SELECT, clara_authenticated:SELECT); the subquery cannot return two rows (uq_membership_active_user is unique on user_id where status='active'); firm_invites keeps zero application-role grants and FORCE RLS; the p_firm_memberships_owner policy (USING true, clara_fn_owner) is what lets both the owner-executed view and the definer function read the issuer's row, so a healthy issuer does not read as lapsed.

issuer_lapsed overriding a settled outcome: the expired arm is evaluated first and both bodies guard on i.status='pending'; accepted/revoked pass through. clara.firm_invites.invited_by is NOT NULL and clara.invite_member is the only writer of the table, so there is no agent-issued invite that would read issuer_lapsed forever.

Downstream readers of the widened status domain: no view or function depends on clara.firm_invites_visible (zero pg_rewrite edges), and no web code filters the roster on status==='pending' except the badge variant, so the fifth value cannot silently drop a row from a count or hide a Revoke control.

#996 misattributed dispositions: byKey is keyed off the DISPOSITION's own client/service_group, and clara.list_review_queue's compliance_rows CTE filters cw.state<>'resolved', so a resolved watch (of which several may share one client/service_group pair) can never overwrite the open one's entry; uq_compliance_watches_one_open guarantees at most one open watch per (client_id, service_group, watch_kind).
#996 reload storm: useAsyncRead reads its loader through a ref and the dispositions reload only writes its OWN state, so the useEffect keyed on `register` cannot re-trigger itself.
Splice anchors: none of 0269/0270/0271 splices a body -- all three are whole create-or-replace or drop, so there is no anchor that could match twice or zero times.

0271 on a database with real rows: the prestate refuses unless the body is byte-identical to its pin, granted to clara_authenticated alone with no PUBLIC entry, with zero pg_depend edges, zero calling triggers and no wake_fn_allowlist row; the drop is `if exists` and the tail re-reads both untouched siblings' bodies and ACLs.

Asia/Kuala_Lumpur vs UTC day: clara._reserve_document_ingest counts its daily window off date_trunc('day', now() at time zone 'utc'), which is what 0270's header claims, so the ceiling's 'one UTC day' wording is accurate.
Integer cents: none of these five tickets touches a money amount.

#871's stop: the two load-bearing claims check out on this branch -- grep -rn service_role packages/db/migrations returns 0 matches across all 234 files, and grep -in invit docs/ARCHITECTURE.md returns 0, which also backs #872's documented deviation from its brief's ARCHITECTURE pointer.
